object.title: Rational-slope $q,t$-Catalan symmetry conjecture
object.statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime positive integers, let $Y_{m,n}$ be the set of lattice paths below the diagonal in an $m$ by $n$ rectangle, and define

$$
c_{m,n}(q,t)=\sum_{D\in Y_{m,n}}q^{\delta-|D|}t^{h_{+}^{\frac{n}{m}}(D)},\qquad \delta=\frac{(m-1)(n-1)}{2},
$$

where $h_{+}^{\frac{n}{m}}(D)$ is the rational-slope arm-and-leg statistic. **Symmetry conjecture.** The function $c_{m,n}(q,t)$ satisfies

$$
c_{m,n}(q,t)=c_{m,n}(t,q).
$$

This is a special case of a conjecture of Loehr and Warrington. The claim is proved for $m=n+1$ and, in the source, for $m\leq 3$; the general coprime case remains open there.
object.source_name: Evgeny Gorsky and Mikhail Mazin, “Compactified Jacobians and q,t-Catalan numbers, II”, arXiv:1204.5448 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.5448

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

object.title: Maffray's bipartisan even-pair conjecture
object.statement: A graph is **bipartisan** if it is Berge, contains no $L(K_{3,3}\setminus e)$ and no double diamond, and neither $G$ nor $\overline{G}$ contains a long prism. An **even pair** is a pair of vertices such that every chordless path between them has even length. **Maffray's conjecture.** If $G$ is bipartisan with at least two vertices, then at least one of $G$ and $\overline{G}$ contains an even pair. This would generalize the bull-free Berge graph theorem and could shorten the proof of the strong perfect graph theorem. The survey presents it as an open conjecture.
object.source_name: Nicolas Trotignon, “Perfect graphs: a survey”, arXiv:1301.5149 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.5149

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2013). “Note that this does not hold for all Berge graphs as shown by $L(K_{3, 3}\setminus e)$ (see Fig. ).”

object.title: Extension conjecture for dense-triangle $K_9$-minor-free graphs
object.statement: A **triangle** is a cycle of length $3$, and a graph is **$K_9$-minor free** if it has no $K_9$ minor. **Dense-triangle $K_9$ extension conjecture.** If every edge of a graph $G$ belongs to at least $7$ triangles, then either $G$ has a $K_9$ minor or $G$ contains $K_{1,2,2,2,2,2}$ as an induced subgraph. This would extend the paper's main theorem to the next minor size and has further consequences for stress freeness and double-critical graphs; the source gives no proof.
object.source_name: Boris Albar and Daniel Gonçalves, “On triangles in K_r-minor free graphs”, arXiv:1304.5468 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5468

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2013). “This conjecture has been proved for $k \leq 5$ but remains open for $k \geq 6$.”

object.title: The minimal excluded minors conjecture for graphs with $g(H)\leq 2$
object.statement:
Let $g(H)$ denote the least integer $k$ such that every $k$-connected $H$-minor-free graph has bounded pathwidth. Let $\mathcal{H}_2$ be the class of graphs $H$ with $g(H)\leq 2$, and let $Q$ be the octahedron graph $K_{2,2,2}$ minus the edges of a triangle. **Minimal excluded minors conjecture.** The minimal excluded minors for $\mathcal{H}_2$ are

$$
\{K_4, K_{2,3}, K_3\cup K_3, Q\}.
$$

The conjecture is equivalent to saying that $g(H)\leq 2$ if and only if $H$ is outerplanar and has a vertex transversal of size at most $1$; its resolution is not given in the source.
object.source_name: Emily A. Marshall and David R. Wood, “Circumference and Pathwidth of Highly Connected Graphs”, arXiv:1309.7683 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.7683

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

object.title: MSOL recognizability conjecture for (3-connected) Hamiltonian partial $k$-trees
object.statement: Fix $k$ and consider partial $k$-trees, namely graphs of treewidth at most $k$, together with the subclass of 3-connected partial $k$-trees. A graph property is **recognizable** if it is recognized by a finite-state tree automaton, and it is **MSOL-definable** if it can be expressed in monadic second-order logic. **The Hamiltonian partial $k$-tree conjecture.** MSOL-definability equals recognizability for Hamiltonian partial $k$-trees, with the 3-connected version included as the source's parenthesized variant. The proposed result is motivated by the existence of an MSOL-definable ordering of nodes with the same parent when the underlying graph has a Hamiltonian path; no resolution is given.
object.source_name: Lars Jaffke and Hans L. Bodlaender, “MSOL-Definability Equals Recognizability for Halin Graphs and Bounded Degree k-Outerplanar Graphs”, arXiv:1503.01604 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01604

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

object.title: Geelen–Gerards–Whittle polynomial-time girth conjecture for proper minor-closed classes
object.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a proper minor-closed class of binary matroids. **Geelen–Gerards–Whittle's conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm for computing the girth of matroids in $\mathcal{M}$. This conjecture connects the tractability of girth computation with structural restrictions on binary matroid classes; the paper studies an algorithmic result for perturbed graphic matroids, while the conjecture concerns every proper minor-closed class of binary matroids.
object.source_name: Jim Geelen and Rohan Kapadia, “Computing girth and cogirth in perturbed graphic matroids”, arXiv:1504.07647 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.07647

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2015).

object.title: The Hamiltonicity bounds for once-subdivided multigraphs
object.statement:
Let $M$ be a multigraph, and let $H$ be obtained from $M$ by subdividing each edge of $M$ at least once. For a positive integer $k$, let $h_k(H)$ denote the least number of colors needed so that every proper $k$-coloring of $H$ has a bichromatic subgraph containing a Hamiltonian cycle. **The Hamiltonicity bounds for once-subdivided multigraphs.** One should have

$$
h_3(H)\leq 2\quad\text{and}\quad h_4(H)=1.
$$

The paper has established related bounds for graphs obtained by subdividing edges at least twice or three times, but indicates that the corresponding statements for $h_k(H)$ should admit improvement; the proposed bounds for one subdivision are not resolved in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Daniel C. McDonald, “Connectedness and Hamiltonicity of graphs on vertex colorings”, arXiv:1507.05344 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05344

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

object.title: Erdős–Gyárfás–Pyber monochromatic cycle partition conjecture
object.statement: Let $r$ be a positive integer, and let an $r$-edge-coloured complete graph be a complete graph whose edges receive one of $r$ colours. **Erdős–Gyárfás–Pyber conjecture.** The vertices of every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be covered with $r$ vertex-disjoint monochromatic cycles. This is the central exact cycle-partition conjecture motivating the paper's approximate results; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Partitioning a graph into a cycle and a sparse graph”, arXiv:1607.03348 (2016).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1509.05539](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.05539), [arXiv:1509.09168](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.09168), [arXiv:1205.5492](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.5492).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03348

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

object.title: Jacobian-dual formulation of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture
object.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph on $n$ vertices, let $G(D)$ be its associated bipartite graph, let $M_D$ be the perfect matching associated with $D$, and let $\phi$ be the Taylor presentation matrix of the edge ideal $I(G(D))$. Write $\overline{B(\phi)}$ for the reduced Jacobian dual, and $I_q(\overline{B(\phi)})$ for its ideal of $q\times q$ minors. **Jacobian-dual formulation of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture.** If every vertex of $D$ has outdegree at least $\dfrac{n}{\ell}$, then for some $q\leq\ell$, the ideal $I_q(\overline{B(\phi)})$ contains a binomial with square-free, relatively prime terms, one of which is a product of elements of $M_D$. By the results established in the paper, this formulation is equivalent to the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture and translates directed-cycle existence into a condition on minors of a reduced Jacobian dual.
object.source_name: Huy Tai Ha and Susan Morey, “Algebraic algorithms for even circuits in graphs”, arXiv:1907.03166 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.03166

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

object.title: Jørgensen's apex conjecture for 6-connected graphs without $K_6$ minors
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and recall that $G$ is **6-connected** if deleting fewer than six vertices leaves it connected, while $G$ is **apex** if it has a vertex $v$ such that $G-v$ is planar. A **$K_6$ minor** is a graph obtained from $G$ by vertex deletions, edge deletions, and simple edge contractions.

**Jørgensen's conjecture.** If $G$ is 6-connected and does not have a $K_6$ minor, then $G$ is apex.

This conjecture, attributed in the source to Jørgensen, is related to Hadwiger's conjecture and concerns the structure of highly connected graphs excluding a complete-graph minor. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Ryan Odeneal and Andrei Pavelescu, “Simple Graphs of Order 12 and Minimum Degree 6 Contain K_6 Minors”, arXiv:1910.11891 (2020).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1203.2192](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2192), [arXiv:1203.2171](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2171).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.11891

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

object.title: Finite boundedness of Ramsey numbers for complete and anisotropic spaces
object.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and let $s,t,\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s,t\geq\ell\geq2$. For an alternating $\ell$-linear map $\phi:(\mathbb{F}^n)^{\times\ell}\to\mathbb{F}^m$, define $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{c}}_{\mathbb{F}}(s,t,\ell)$ as the least $n$ such that every such map has either a totally isotropic space of dimension $s$ or a complete space of dimension $t$. Define $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{a}}_{\mathbb{F}}(s,t,\ell)$ similarly, replacing complete spaces by anisotropic spaces.

**Ramsey-number conjecture.** The Ramsey numbers for complete spaces and anisotropic spaces, $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{c}}_{\mathbb{F}}(s,t,\ell)$ and $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{a}}_{\mathbb{F}}(s,t,\ell)$, are upper bounded by explicit functions in $s$, $t$, and $\ell$.

At present, finite upper bounds are not known for general $\ell$. The conjecture asks for explicit bounds analogous to those in hypergraph Ramsey theory, despite the additional linear-algebraic correlations that obstruct the usual recursive arguments.
object.source_name: Youming Qiao, “Turán and Ramsey problems for alternating multilinear maps”, arXiv:2007.12820 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.12820

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

object.title: Infinite Mader theorem for internally vertex-disjoint T-paths
object.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a possibly infinite graph and let $T\subseteq V$. An internally vertex-disjoint $T$-path system is accompanied by $X\subseteq V\setminus T$ and a partition $\mathcal{Y}$ of $V\setminus(T\cup X)$. For each $Y\in\mathcal{Y}$, define

$$
B_Y=\\{v\in Y: v\text{ has a neighbour in }V\setminus(X\cup Y)\\}.
$$

After deleting $X$ and all edges inside the parts $Y$, no $T$-path remains; the paths cover $X$ and all but at most one vertex of each $B_Y$. Each path either meets $X$ once and each $B_Y$ at most once, or meets $X$ not at all, meets one uniquely determined $B_Y$ twice, and every other $B_Y$ at most once; moreover, at most one path meets each $B_Y$ exactly once.

**Mader's internally-disjoint-path conjecture.** Such a system $\mathcal{P}$, set $X$, and partition $\mathcal{Y}$ exist.

This is proposed as an infinite complementary-slackness analogue of Mader's finite minimax theorem for internally vertex-disjoint $T$-paths. No resolution is given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Attila Joó, “The Lovász-Cherkassky theorem in countable graphs”, arXiv:2102.04203 (2021).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.04203

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

object.title: Total positivity of the Schl"afli--Gessel--Seo polynomial matrix and sequences
object.statement: For $n,k\geq 0$, let $P_{n,k}(a,b)$ be the Schl"afli--Gessel--Seo forest polynomials, let $P_n(x;a,b)=\sum_{k=0}^n P_{n,k}(a,b)x^k$, and let $P_n(a,b)=P_{n,1}(a,b)$. A polynomial matrix or sequence is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all its minors have coefficientwise nonnegative polynomial coefficients; a sequence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive when all minors of its Hankel matrix have this property. **Total positivities for the Schl"afli--Gessel--Seo polynomials.** (a) The unit-lower-triangular polynomial matrix $P(a,b)=\bigl(P_{n,k}(a,b)\bigr)_{n,k\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise totally positive jointly in $a,b$. (b) The polynomial sequence ${\bm{P}}=\bigl(P_n(x;a,b)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive jointly in $x,a,b$. (c) The polynomial sequence ${\bm{P}}^\triangle=\bigl(P_{n+1,1}(a,b)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive jointly in $a,b$. These claims extend known total-positivity phenomena for forest triangles and their row-generating polynomials; the source gives no resolution and presents them as conjectures.
object.source_name: Alan D. Sokal, “Total positivity of some polynomial matrices that enumerate labeled trees and forests, I. Forests of rooted labeled trees”, arXiv:2105.05583 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05583

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

object.title: Total positivity of bivariate functional-digraph polynomials
object.statement: Let $\Psi_n(x,y)$ be the generating polynomial for functional digraphs on $[n]$, with weight $x$ for each cyclic vertex and weight $y$ for each component. Define $\psi^{\rm X}_{n,k}(y)=[x^k]\Psi_n(x,y)$ and $\psi^{\rm Y}_{n,k}(x)=[y^k]\Psi_n(x,y)$. A polynomial matrix is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all minors have coefficientwise nonnegative coefficients; a polynomial sequence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive when all Hankel minors have coefficientwise nonnegative coefficients. **Total positivities for the bivariate functional-digraph polynomials.** (a) The unit-lower-triangular matrix $\Psi^{\rm Y}=\bigl(\psi^{\rm Y}_{n,k}(x)\bigr)_{n,k\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise totally positive in $x$. (b) The sequence ${\bm{\Psi}}=\bigl(\Psi_n(x,y)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $x,y$. (c) ${\bm{\Psi}}^{{\rm Y}\triangle}=\bigl(\psi^{\rm Y}_{n+1,1}\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $x$. The claims extend the known positivity of the other coefficient matrix and its one-component column; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Alan D. Sokal, “Total positivity of some polynomial matrices that enumerate labeled trees and forests, I. Forests of rooted labeled trees”, arXiv:2105.05583 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05583

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

object.title: Total positivity of bivariate forest polynomials
object.statement: Let $f^\sharp_{n,k}(w)$ be the entries of the exponential Riordan array with generating function $G(t)=(e^{wT(t)}-1)/w$, where $T(t)$) is the tree function, and define $F_n^\sharp(x,w)=\sum_{k=0}^n f^\sharp_{n,k}(w)x^k$. A polynomial matrix is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all minors have coefficientwise nonnegative coefficients; a polynomial sequence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive when all Hankel minors have coefficientwise nonnegative coefficients. **Total positivities for the bivariate forest polynomials.** (a) $F^\sharp=\bigl(f^\sharp_{n,k}(w)\bigr)_{n,k\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise totally positive in $w$. (b) ${\bm{F}}^\sharp=\bigl(F_n^\sharp(x,w)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $x,w$. (c) ${\bm{F}}^{\sharp\triangle}=\bigl(f^\sharp_{n+1,1}(w)\bigr)_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $w$. The source verifies parts (a) and (b) only to finite orders and notes that (c) follows from (b); no general proof is given.
object.source_name: Alan D. Sokal, “Total positivity of some polynomial matrices that enumerate labeled trees and forests, I. Forests of rooted labeled trees”, arXiv:2105.05583 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.05583

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

object.title: Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall List Total Coloring Conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $T(G)$ be its total graph, whose vertices are the vertices and edges of $G$, with adjacency given by adjacency, incidence, or edge adjacency in $G$. The source also writes $T(G)=B(G)^2$. Write $\chi$ for chromatic number and $\chi_\ell$ for list chromatic number. **Borodin–Kostochka–Woodall List Total Coloring Conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi(T(G))=\chi_\ell(T(G)).
$$

This conjecture is a special case of the stronger List Square Coloring Conjecture, which has been refuted by Kim and Park; consequently, the total-coloring conjecture is refuted as stated.
object.source_name: Morteza Hasanvand, “The List Square Coloring Conjecture fails for bipartite planar graphs and their line graphs”, arXiv:2211.00622 (2025).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1305.2566](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.2566).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00622

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2022). “In 2015 Kim and Park disproved this conjecture for non-bipartite and bipartite graphs.”

object.title: Everett–Reed's conjecture on even-contractile Berge graphs
object.statement: Let $G$ be a **Berge graph**, meaning a graph with no induced odd hole and no induced odd antihole. An **antihole** is the complement of a hole, and an **odd prism** is a prism whose three rungs all have an odd number of edges. A graph is **even-contractile** if it can be reduced to a single vertex by contracting edges whose endpoints have no common neighbor. **Everett–Reed's conjecture.** If $G$ has no induced subgraph isomorphic to an antihole of length at least six or to an odd prism, then $G$ is even-contractile. This conjecture concerns a proposed characterization of even-contractile Berge graphs and remains open, although several related theorems have been proved.
object.source_name: Tara Abrishami, Maria Chudnovsky and Yaqian Tang, “Even pairs in Berge graphs with no balanced skew-partitions”, arXiv:2305.00532 (2024).
object.references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2303.12824](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12824), [arXiv:1502.03695](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03695), [arXiv:1309.0435](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0435), [arXiv:1309.0438](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0438), [arXiv:1301.5149](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.5149).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00532

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2023). “This conjecture remains open, but several related theorems have been proved.”

object.title: Hartsfield–Ringel antimagic graph conjecture
object.statement: A finite, simple, undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ has an **antimagic labelling** if a bijection $f:E\to\{1,2,\ldots,|E|\}$ gives each vertex $u$ the sum of labels on its incident edges, with all vertex-sums pairwise distinct. **Hartsfield–Ringel conjecture.** Every connected graph other than $K_2$ is antimagic. This is the foundational conjecture on antimagic labellings; the source does not state its current resolution status.
object.source_name: Grégoire Beaudoire, Cédric Bentz and Christophe Picouleau, “Antimagic labelling of graphs with maximum degree Δ(G) = n - 4”, arXiv:2603.02956 (2026).
object.references:
**15 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2512.17693](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17693), [arXiv:2507.17302](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17302), [arXiv:2503.15296](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15296), [arXiv:2408.11931](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11931), [arXiv:2405.05375](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05375), [arXiv:2402.10472](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10472), [arXiv:2308.07278](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07278), [arXiv:2209.08408](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.08408), [arXiv:2112.13582](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.13582), [arXiv:1812.06715](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06715), [arXiv:1712.09477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09477), [arXiv:1708.00624](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00624), and 2 more.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02956

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026).

object.title: Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture
object.statement:
Let $[n]:=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For $k\geq 3$, a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ is **$k$-sunflower free** if it contains no $k$ pairwise distinct sets whose pairwise intersections are all equal. In the uniform setting, every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has size $m$. **Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture.** For $k\geq 3$, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $k$-sunflower free family of $m$-subsets of $[n]$. Then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \mu^m
$$

for a constant $\mu$ depending only on $k$. This is the uniform sunflower conjecture for set systems; the paper presents it as the conjecture introduced by Erdős and Rado, while the supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Omran Ahmadi and Hassan Norouzi, “A Polynomial Improvement of Naslund–Sawin Bound for Sunflower-Free Families Using Triangular Tensors”, arXiv:2606.30593 (2026).
object.references:
**13 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.02667](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02667), [arXiv:2605.12232](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12232), [arXiv:2605.21208](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21208), [arXiv:2310.15527](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15527), [arXiv:2307.01374](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01374), [arXiv:1908.08483](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08483), [arXiv:1903.00580](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.00580), [arXiv:1804.10050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.10050), [arXiv:1702.02831](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02831), [arXiv:1606.09575](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.09575), [arXiv:1601.04897](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.04897), [arXiv:1411.4692](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4692).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30593

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

object.title: Sokal's Hankel-total positivity conjecture for GKP row-generating polynomials
object.statement: Let $P_n(x;\bm{\mu})$ be the row-generating polynomials of the Graham–Knuth–Patashnik recurrence, with parameters $\bm{\mu}=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\alpha',\beta',\gamma')$ treated as indeterminates. Thus the coefficientwise partial order is taken in the seven variables $x,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\alpha',\beta',\gamma'$ on ${\mathbb Z}[x,\bm{\mu}]$. A sequence $(a_n)_{n\geq 0}$ is **Hankel-totally positive** when every minor of its Hankel matrix $(a_{i+j})_{i,j\geq 0}$ is nonnegative in this order. **Sokal's conjecture.** The sequence $(P_n(x;\bm{\mu}))_{n\geq 0}$ of row-generating polynomials of the GKP recurrence is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive, jointly in all seven indeterminates $x$ and $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\alpha',\beta',\gamma'$. This conjecture concerns total positivity of the Hankel matrix formed from the GKP row-generating polynomials and remains open.
object.source_name: Jesús Salas, “Log-concavity and log-convexity in the theory of the Graham–Knuth–Patashnik recurrences”, arXiv:2607.04217 (2026).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2202.03793](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03793).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04217

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “This conjecture is still open.”
